collections.description: A published work written by one author.
A registered customer who places orders.

properties.name: Email
properties.description: Login email of the customer, unique across customers.

collections.description: A purchase placed by a customer.
One product line within an order. It cannot exist without its order.

properties.name: Line number
properties.description: Position of the line within the order.

properties.name: Quantity
properties.description: Number of units ordered on this line.

collections.description: A company that supplies goods to the business.

properties.name: Supplier name
properties.description: Current trading name of the supplier.

collections.description: A purchase order issued to a supplier. It keeps a copy of the supplier name as it was when the order was issued.

properties.name: Purchase order ID
properties.description: Unique identifier of the purchase order.

properties.name: Supplier name
properties.description: Copy of the supplier name at the time of issue.

collections.description: A course taught in a specific term.
A student's registration in one course offering.
An organizational unit that employees belong to.
A person employed by the company.
A piece of work carried out by one or more employees.
The assignment of an employee to a project, with the role they play on it.

properties.name: Project ID
properties.description: Project the employee is assigned to.

properties.name: Role
properties.description: Role the employee plays on the project.

buckets.name: Entity to entity
buckets.description: Conceptual relationships between business entities. Ends name whole entities, so only the reading direction, roles, and verbs are defined here.

buckets.name: Foreign key
buckets.description: Foreign keys link child attributes to the primary key of a parent entity, with delete and update rules and cardinalities.

buckets.name: Foreign master
buckets.description: A foreign master records that the child stores a copy of the parent's value rather than a reference to it.

buckets.name: Composite relationship
buckets.description: Composite FK example: enrollment foreign keys match the composite PK of course offering.

buckets.name: Human resources
buckets.description: Employees, the departments they belong to, and the projects they work on.

relationships.name: Author books
relationships.description: An author writes many books; each book is written by one author.

relationships.name: Book publisher
relationships.description: A book is published by one publisher; a publisher publishes many books. Read in both directions.

relationships.name: Order customer
relationships.description: Each order is placed by exactly one customer; a customer may place many orders. Enforced by a non-identifying foreign key.

relationships.name: Order line order
relationships.description: Each order line belongs to exactly one order; an order contains one or more lines. The foreign key is part of the order line's primary key, so the relationship is identifying.

relationships.name: Purchase order supplier name
relationships.description: Each purchase order stores a copy of its supplier's name. The copy is not updated when the supplier record changes.

relationships.name: Enrollment course offering
relationships.description: Composite FK: Course code + Term code. Identifying.

relationships.name: Employee department
relationships.description: Each employee belongs to exactly one department; a department has many employees.

relationships.name: Assignment employee
relationships.description: Each assignment concerns exactly one employee.

relationships.name: Assignment project
relationships.description: Each assignment is on exactly one project.
